Secure-by-default: no secret anywhere in the code (the bot user id and connection id are not secrets); the agent reply and the use case names are escaped before they go to Slack (a '<!' becomes '<!', so a reply or name cannot ping @channel); writes set single fields only (rule 4); the owner check on the approve branch compares the row's owner_slack_id with the event's user, read from psl_poc in the same run (rule 3).
unverified: Security: the Slack webhook URL of this automation was not obtained: the trigger's webhookUrl is filled by a builder-panel loader, open_workflow does not return it and no automation-code tool does. It stays out of this report. The person reads it from the trigger panel after the deploy and pastes it into the Slack app (Event Subscriptions), where the bot must be subscribed to message.channels (and message.groups for private channels) and member_joined_channel.

Security: whether the platform verifies Slack's request signature or verification token on this webhook is not shown. The listener trusts event.user for the owner check on the approve branch; anyone who learns the webhook URL could forge an event. Check: ask the platform owner whether the Slack trigger verifies the signing secret, and keep the URL private.

The four arms' working paths were not run, because each makes a real effect the task did not authorise: the join arm writes psl_poc rows and posts in Slack, the tag and manager-reply arms call the POC Studio Agent (model cost, and its tool can create a psl_poc row) and post in Slack, the approve arm calls Approve gate. Check: in a test channel, add the bot, tag it with a use case name, reply in the manager thread and reply 'approve' under a gate post, then read psl_poc, psl_activity and the thread.

slack_live is set from a Groovy step's boolean output, because the compiler refuses the literal true for setValue (INVALID_INPUT_TYPE). Whether the row stores a boolean true, not the string 'true', is not seen. Check: after a real join, get_records on psl_poc for slack_live and filter eq slack_live true.

slack_last_ts is written as a Slack-style ts built from the run clock ('<seconds>.<6 digits>', for example 1792134224.866000). Whether Read channels into History (agent-3) reads slack_last_ts in that form is not checked.

The three slack_post_message_in_channel nodes carry token_type bot_token as the task says; that operation does not declare it, so the save warned inputs.unknownKey. Slack answers refused calls as data ({ok false, error ...}) with a completed node, as the unknown-channel runs showed for the read nodes; the post nodes' ok is not checked, so a refused post ends the path without a retry. Check: one real post with and without token_type.

A Slack retry is stopped by a bot reply later than the event in the same thread; a retry that arrives while the first run's agent call is still running can still answer twice. event_id is not used. The answered check reads at most 50 replies (tag arm) or 200 (manager arm).

A tag in a thread reply, a tag by the bot itself, and any other event type are ignored; a reply that says 'approve' with other words, or 'Approve!' with punctuation, is treated as an ordinary manager-thread reply (no row matches, so it ends). Messages with a subtype other than thread_broadcast and file_share are ignored.
The join arm reads at most 100 psl_poc rows of that channel name; the manager-thread lookup at most 20 rows.
notes: handover: Slack listener workflow id 6ad1cc2a300f9003500f1da3, saved version 0, NOT deployed (deployment null), trigger slack_on_new_message on connection 6ad1be602ac9ba64653a9d36 (event trigger: no input keys and no result keys; it ends with stop()). Deploy it, then read its webhook URL from the trigger panel and paste it into the Slack app's Event Subscriptions; until then no Slack event reaches it. It calls the AI agent e_6ad1ca0bc0f97b3e983d2679 through ai_agents_by_unifyapps_invoke_agent and Approve gate 6ad1c75967956c53e38f1a70 (role owner) through callables_call_automation, which runs the deployed copy: Approve gate is still its shell until its logic task deploys.

assumed: the 'invoke-agent node' is ai_agents_by_unifyapps_invoke_agent (its default fallback workflow is the invoke-agent callable 68050ca67df58855654804a0 the task names), not a bare callables_call_automation node; the reply is read from publicResponse[0].text.

assumed: when the agent answers nothing or its call fails, the tag arm posts 'I could not work that out just now. Please tag me again.' and the manager-reply arm 'I could not work that out just now. Please reply again.', so a person is not left without an answer; the agent node runs with onError CONTINUE for this.

assumed: a 'tag' is a top-level message (no thread_ts, or thread_ts equal to ts) whose text contains <@U0C9P6MFR62>; 'approve' means the whole text, trimmed and case-folded, equals 'approve'; the gate post's first line is matched with [POC-<letters, digits, . _ ->] and its author must be the bot.
assumed: the approve arm only calls Approve gate and posts nothing in Slack, as the contract says; the owner is told nothing if Approve gate answers forbidden or already_decided.

assumed: for a manager reply the agent gets the row's channel name from psl_poc.slack_channel, and the tagged Slack ids travel inside the text, as the agent's instructions read the manager from the tag in the text.

The Slack read nodes (get conversation, list replies) and the agent call run with onError CONTINUE; the post nodes, the row updates, the fetches and the Approve gate call stop the run on failure. The trigger's filter is also applied in the test run, so bot-authored events end at the Trigger node there; the classify step repeats the bot and subtype checks for events that reach the body.

feedback:
Bug: `compile_and_save_workflow` refuses a boolean literal as `setValue` of `storage_by_unifyapps_update_record_fields_by_id`, so a boolean field (psl_poc.slack_live) cannot be set with `setValue: true`.
Context: Building automation 6ad1cc2a300f9003500f1da3 (POC Studio Live · Slack listener); updateFields `{ fieldName: "properties.slack_live", actionType: "SET", setValue: true }` on object psl_poc, where slack_live is a boolean.
Where: mcp-tool
Evidence: save answered `INVALID_INPUT_TYPE ... updateFields[1].setValue is a boolean but the schema expects a string`; nothing saved. Worked around by passing a Groovy node's boolean output as a pill (`setValue: classify.result.live`), which compiled; what is stored at run time was not read back.
Cause: Unknown — next check: run the saved node on a throwaway psl_poc row and read slack_live back with get_records (boolean true versus string "true").
Regression: Save an update_record_fields_by_id node that SETs a boolean field, run it on a test row, and read the field back as a boolean.

feature:
Feature: A tool that returns the webhook URL of an automation's appEvent trigger (for example slack_on_new_message), for the person to paste into the Slack app.
Evidence: The trigger's `webhookUrl` field is filled by a builder-panel loader (`getWebhookUrl`); `open_workflow` returns no webhookUrl in the saved trigger and no automation-code tool calls that loader, so the URL could not be put in the report.
Benefit: Every build with a Slack, GitHub or other event trigger needs this hand-over step; today it is done by hand in the browser.
Scope: automation-code MCP tools (open_workflow or a new read tool); not changing how webhooks are registered.
Acceptance: Calling the tool with a saved appEvent automation's id returns its webhook URL string.
